countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.
countries.metaTitle: Study in India: Guide for International Students
countries.metaDescription: Regulators, admission routes, entrance tests, student visa and FRRO rules that international applicants should verify before applying to an Indian university.

Programmes in this category are built around a sequence of architectural design studios supported by building construction, structures, history and theory, environmental services, urban design and professional practice, and normally include a practical training period and a final thesis project. courses.name: Bachelor of Business Administration
courses.summary: The Bachelor of Business Administration is an undergraduate management degree taken after secondary school. Core study covers accounting, finance, marketing, organisational behaviour, human resource management, operations, business law and economics, usually followed by a specialisation such as business analytics, international business, digital marketing, finance or healthcare management, plus an internship or live project. Programmes run for three years in many systems and four years where an honours or research year is added. Graduates move into entry-level management roles or continue to an MBA or a specialist master's degree.

Typical coursework covers programming languages, data structures, database systems, operating systems, computer networks, web and mobile development, software engineering and discrete mathematics, with electives in areas such as data science, cyber security or cloud computing. The degree usually lasts three years, or four with an honours or research year, and commonly leads to software and IT roles or to a Master of Computer Applications.

It is usually a four-year programme entered after secondary school with physics, chemistry and mathematics or biology. Graduates work in biopharmaceutical, food, agricultural and environmental biotechnology or continue to M.Tech or research study.

universities.name: Manipal University Jaipur
universities.summary: Manipal University Jaipur (MUJ) is a self-financed state private university set up under Rajasthan Act No. 21 of 2011 and part of the Manipal Education and Medical Group. Its 122-acre campus is at Dehmi Kalan, off the Jaipur-Ajmer Expressway. It teaches engineering, architecture, design, hospitality, law, management, sciences, pharmacy, psychology and media in English.
universities.campusLifestyle: MUJ opened in 2011 on 122 acres allotted at Dehmi Kalan village. The air-conditioned Central Library (2,319 sq m, 700 seats) holds about 57,800 books and 400 print journals, subscribes to e-resources including IEEE, ScienceDirect, JSTOR and Manupatra, and opens 8.30 am to 11 pm on weekdays. The hostel zone has a gym, laundry, cafeterias, a store and a salon, and sports facilities cover football, hockey, basketball, volleyball, tennis and badminton. Students need 75 per cent attendance in each course to sit its end-semester exam.
universities.cityProfile: The campus address is Dehmi Kalan, off the Jaipur-Ajmer Expressway, Jaipur, Rajasthan 303007, on the edge of Rajasthan's capital. MUJ gives these distances: Jaipur Airport at Sanganer 27 km, Jaipur Railway Station 24 km and the Jaipur bus stand 25 km, with prepaid taxis from the station. Jaipur Airport has domestic flights to cities including Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Goa. Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation buses run between Jaipur and Delhi about every half hour and take about six hours; the drive from Delhi takes about five. Hostel residents need the Chief Warden's approval and parental consent to go into the city by day, and must be back by 9 pm.
universities.practicalExposure: NBA's Tier I (Washington Accord) register lists MUJ's B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering as accredited to 30 June 2027. Two B.Tech programmes, Computer Science and Engineering and Civil Engineering, run as 2+2 dual degrees with Deakin University, Australia: two years at MUJ and two at Deakin, where MUJ lists tuition of about AUD 42,000 and AUD 45,000 a year respectively. The B.Tech CSE adds project-based learning from semester three and electives from semester four, and MUJ's academic rules give the eighth B.Tech semester and the third and fourth M.Tech semesters to project work. MUJ's Directorate of International Collaborations lists partner universities in countries including Malaysia, Malta, Nepal, Russia and Kazakhstan, and its International Student Cell runs semester exchanges, internships, study tours and summer and winter schools. The two-year residential MBA is run by the TAPMI School of Business at MUJ.
universities.hostelOverview: Separate men's (blocks B1-B10) and women's (G1-G7) hostels are on campus, run by Good Host Spaces. For 2026-27 a double room costs INR 167,372 plus INR 15,378 housekeeping and a refundable INR 25,475 deposit: INR 208,225 a year, paid in advance. Mess membership (INR 79,000 for 2026-27) is compulsory for residents. Optional laundry is INR 8,810 and the gym INR 12,750. Rooms are air-conditioned and furnished; single rooms depend on availability. The contract runs a full year and fees are non-refundable once it starts.
universities.dietarySupport: The hostel mess serves vegetarian food, with separately cooked non-vegetarian meals on selected days. Two caterers, Bluspring Indya Foods and BlueDove, run the messes; students choose through the SpaceBasic app and can switch every two months. The mess fee may be revised in-year if food costs rise. Cafeterias, food courts and a departmental store operate in the hostel area, and vendor outlets deliver to blocks from 11 pm to 2 am.
universities.safetyOverview: Men's and women's hostels have separate entrances, 24-hour security and a warden and caretakers in each block. A resident doctor and an ambulance are on the hostel premises, and students are taken to hospital when needed. MUJ names an anti-ragging committee for 2026-27 under UGC regulations, and a proctorial board and grievance redressal committee handle discipline cases.
universities.studentSupport: MUJ's Office of International Admissions (admissions@jaipur.manipal.edu, toll-free 1800 102 0128) handles Foreign, NRI, PIO and OCI applicants and issues the letter for the student visa. The Directorate of Student Welfare offers individual and group counselling, and the hostel operator runs separate helplines for the men's and women's hostels.

faq.question: Is Manipal University Jaipur public or private?
faq.answer: It is a self-financed state private university, established by Rajasthan Act No. 21 of 2011 and launched that year at the invitation of the Government of Rajasthan. UGC lists it among state private universities in Rajasthan. MUJ belongs to the Manipal Education and Medical Group but is a separate university from Manipal Academy of Higher Education in Karnataka.

faq.question: What language are programmes taught in?
faq.answer: MUJ's Academic Rules and Regulations state that the medium of instruction for all courses offered is English. There is no switch to Hindi later in the degree.

faq.question: Do international applicants take an entrance exam or an English test?
faq.answer: MUJ's international guide says international students do not take the entrance examination set for resident Indian students; admission is on qualifying-examination marks. MUJ publishes no IELTS or TOEFL minimum. Some programmes list their own requirements: NATA or an equivalent for B.Arch, CAT, MAT, CMAT, XAT or GMAT for the MBA, and MUJ written tests for the LLM and M.Sc. Clinical Psychology.

faq.question: What are the academic entry requirements?
faq.answer: They vary by programme. B.Tech needs Physics, Mathematics and English at 10+2, A Level, IB or equivalent, with at least 60 per cent across the science subjects on MUJ's merit route (70 per cent for CSE). B.A. English and Liberal Arts need 50 per cent in any stream, BBA (Hons) and B.Com (Hons) 60 per cent, and BHM 45 per cent. Most master's programmes need a relevant bachelor's degree with 50 per cent.

faq.question: How much does it cost per year?
faq.answer: Tuition is published in US dollars per year: USD 7,700 for B.Tech, USD 8,580 for B.Arch, USD 6,000 for B.Pharm, USD 5,500 for BHM, USD 4,400 for most M.Tech programmes and USD 13,200-13,500 for the MBAs. A one-time USD 300 registration fee is added. A double hostel room costs INR 208,225 for 2026-27, including a refundable deposit, plus INR 79,000 for the compulsory mess.

faq.question: How do I apply?
faq.answer: Contact MUJ's Office of International Admissions at admissions@jaipur.manipal.edu or use the International Admissions link on the programme page, and submit your qualifying-examination results. The Committee for Foreign/NRI Admissions recommends admission on those marks. MUJ then issues a letter for the student visa and forwards your details to the Government of India for a No Objection Certificate.

faq.question: When is the intake?
faq.answer: Foreign and NRI students are admitted at the start of the academic year in July or August; the 2026-27 odd semester runs from July to December 2026. Programme pages show international applications for the current cycle as closed, and MUJ has not published a closing date for the next cycle, so apply early in the year.

faq.question: How many seats are there for international students?
faq.answer: MUJ admits foreign citizens, PIO and OCI card holders on up to 15 per cent of approved intake as supernumerary seats, and NRI or NRI-sponsored candidates on up to 5 per cent within the intake. A student stays in the category they were admitted under for the whole programme.

faq.question: What visa and registration steps apply?
faq.answer: Foreign students need a student visa valid for more than 180 days, obtained with MUJ's admission letter. The Bureau of Immigration requires FRRO registration within 14 days of arrival and bars employment and business on a student visa. OCI and PIO card holders do not need a student visa, though PIO card holders must still register with the FRRO.

faq.question: What is MUJ's accreditation status?
faq.answer: NAAC accredited MUJ A+ (CGPA 3.28) in Cycle 1, declared in February 2020, and it remains on NAAC's valid-accreditation list as on 14 August 2025. NBA's Tier I (Washington Accord) register lists B.Tech CSE and IT to 30 June 2027. The Council of Architecture lists the B.Arch as approved for 2026-27. NIRF 2025 ranks MUJ 58th among universities.

faq.question: What accommodation is available?
faq.answer: Separate on-campus hostels for men and women offer air-conditioned double rooms at INR 208,225 a year for 2026-27, including housekeeping and a refundable INR 25,475 deposit, paid in advance for a full-year contract. Mess membership at INR 79,000 is compulsory. Single rooms depend on availability, and some men's rooms are triple for the first semester and double for the second.

faq.question: Can I get a refund if I withdraw?
faq.answer: MUJ follows UGC refund rules: a full refund if you withdraw 15 days or more before the notified last date of admission (the day before orientation), falling to 90, 80 and 50 per cent and then nothing more than 30 days after it. For Foreign and NRI students, refunds follow foreign-exchange rules at the prevailing rate. Hostel fees are non-refundable once the academic year begins.

faq.question: How does MUJ compare with Manipal Academy of Higher Education?
faq.answer: Both belong to the Manipal group, but they are separate universities: MUJ is a Rajasthan state private university on one Jaipur campus, while MAHE is a deemed university in Karnataka. MUJ ranks 58th and MAHE 3rd in the NIRF 2025 University category. Compare each programme's published fee and entry rules rather than the shared name.

admissionsContent.overview: The LLM - Intellectual Property Law runs for 1 year and is taught in English at Manipal University Jaipur's campus at Dehmi Kalan, Jaipur. MUJ's eligibility table lists qualifying marks and an MUJ written entrance test.

eligibility.intro: Entry needs an LL.B. from a recognised university with at least 50 per cent aggregate.
items: A bachelor's degree in law (LL.B.) from a recognised university
At least 50 per cent aggregate marks in the law degree

applicationSteps: Contact MUJ's Office of International Admissions at admissions@jaipur.manipal.edu, or use the International Admissions 'Apply Now' link on the programme page
Submit your qualifying-examination results; the Committee for Foreign/NRI Admissions recommends admission on those marks
On confirmation, receive MUJ's letter for the Indian student visa; MUJ forwards admitted students' details to the Government of India for a No Objection Certificate
Pay the first-year tuition and the one-time registration fee, then book campus housing if wanted
Arrive on a student visa valid for more than 180 days and register with the FRRO within 14 days of arrival

application: Passport
MUJ admission letter issued for the student visa
Indian student visa valid for more than 180 days, or an OCI / PIO card

admissionsContent.deadlinesNote: MUJ admits Foreign and NRI students at the start of the academic year in July or August. The programme page shows international applications for the current cycle as closed, and no next-cycle closing date is published.
visaConsiderations: A student visa valid for more than 180 days is needed, with FRRO registration within 14 days of arrival
OCI and PIO card holders do not need a student visa, but PIO card holders must still register with the FRRO

programmes.feeNotes: MUJ lists international tuition of USD 1,680 a year plus a one-time USD 300 registration fee (USD 1,980 due at admission). Over 1 year that is USD 1,680 in tuition, before any revision: MUJ says fees are subject to its Fee Fixation Committee, and the page prints no academic year. Campus housing for 2026-27 is INR 208,225 a year for a double room (including a refundable INR 25,475 deposit), plus INR 79,000 compulsory mess charges.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
evidence.internalNotes: The qualifying-exam basis has changed between cycles (SAT in earlier cycles, JEE Main for 2026-27). Never state the accepted exam without naming the admission year. Corroborated by dasanit.org, which describes DASA as an MoE scheme for Foreign Nationals, PIOs, OCIs and NRIs to NITs, CFTIs and other premier technical institutions other than IITs.

evidence.claimText: Non-Resident Indians, Overseas Citizens of India and Foreign Nationals are eligible to appear in NEET (UG) and are eligible for admission to medical and dental colleges subject to the rules of the respective State Governments, institutions and the Government of India. Foreign applicants must upload documentary proof of nationality with the application and are directed to confirm eligibility with the competent state and counselling authorities.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Bulletin NEET (UG)-2026, National Testing Agency
evidence.internalNotes: Chapter 6, sections 1-2. No India medical page may present a NEET-free route. Eligibility is explicitly conditional on state and institution rules, so it varies by college.

evidence.claimText: The National Assessment and Accreditation Council, established in 1994 as an autonomous institution of the UGC, assesses and accredits Indian higher education institutions. The National Institutional Ranking Framework, launched by the Ministry of Education in September 2015, is the government ranking framework for Indian institutions.
evidence.sourceLabel: NAAC - official site
evidence.internalNotes: NIRF corroborated separately at https://www.nirfindia.org/Home (MoE, launched 29 September 2015). Use a NAAC grade or NIRF rank only with the assessment or ranking year stated.

evidence.claimText: The UGC publishes a list of fake universities alongside its lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, so institutional recognition must be checked against UGC records before an Indian institution is presented as degree-awarding.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission - Higher Education Institutions listings
evidence.internalNotes: Operational rule for this catalogue: no Indian university is published without a verifiable UGC listing and, where applicable, AICTE approval or NMC recognition.

evidence.claimText: India spans Himalayan, tropical coastal, semi-arid and monsoon-affected climate zones, with the southwest monsoon typically running from June to September.
evidence.sourceLabel: India Meteorological Department, Ministry of Earth Sciences
evidence.internalNotes: General climatic framing only; do not present city-level weather claims at country level.
